subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 7-year-old boy has had a chronic productive cough and recurrent otitis media since infancy. He has had three episodes of pneumonia, and chest imaging shows left lower lobe bronchiectasis. His electrocardiogram shows dextrocardia, and abdominal ultrasound shows the liver on the left side. Sweat chloride testing and serum immunoglobulins are normal. Nasal nitric oxide is measured as a screening test.
question: Which of the following results is most likely, and what is the best explanation?

options.text: Markedly elevated nasal nitric oxide, because neutrophil infiltration increases inducible nitric oxide synthase activity
Normal nasal nitric oxide, because nitric oxide production is unaffected in ciliary disorders
Markedly decreased nasal nitric oxide, because nitric oxide is synthesized by nitric oxide synthase in the sinonasal epithelium and its production falls when ciliary function is impaired
Markedly decreased nasal nitric oxide, because nitric oxide synthase requires vitamin C, which is deficient in this condition
Elevated nasal nitric oxide, because arginine is converted to nitric oxide as a compensatory response to infection

explanation_correct: This boy has primary ciliary dyskinesia with Kartagener syndrome, characterized by situs inversus, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis from defective dynein arms and immotile cilia. Nitric oxide is synthesized from arginine by nitric oxide synthase in the sinonasal epithelium, and nasal nitric oxide is characteristically low in primary ciliary dyskinesia, so measurement of nasal nitric oxide is used as a screening test. The disorder also causes infertility and hearing loss.

explanation_incorrect.A: Inflammation may modestly alter local nitric oxide production, but markedly elevated nasal nitric oxide is not the pattern of primary ciliary dyskinesia.
explanation_incorrect.B: Nitric oxide production is not normal in this disorder; a low nasal nitric oxide level is the characteristic screening finding.
explanation_incorrect.D: Nitric oxide synthase does not require vitamin C; it requires oxygen, NADPH, tetrahydrobiopterin, FAD, FMN, and calmodulin, and the low nasal nitric oxide reflects impaired epithelial function rather than vitamin deficiency.
explanation_incorrect.E: Arginine is the substrate for nitric oxide synthase, but infection does not produce the characteristic elevation of nasal nitric oxide in this disorder.

educationalObjective: Decreased nasal nitric oxide is a screening finding in primary ciliary dyskinesia because nitric oxide is produced by nitric oxide synthase in the sinonasal epithelium.
